title: VPC networking Terraform module: subnet tiering, egress gateway abstraction, endpoint affinity and upgrade hooks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a modular Terraform module that provides opinionated yet configurable VPC networking primitives for Private/VPC deployments. The module will cover subnet tiering (control, workload, infra), multi-AZ NAT/IGW egress abstraction, VPC endpoint provisioning with affinity-aware routing, route table orchestration, and upgrade hooks that enable safe in-place upgrades and synthetic health checks during rolling changes.

Context & motivation:
Private deployments currently rely on multiple ad-hoc Terra modules and scripts across accounts. Customers deploying Redwood Private ask for a repeatable, auditable, and upgrade-safe networking module that: (1) simplifies creating AZ-aware subnet topology, (2) standardizes egress (NAT vs IGW) with predictable failover, (3) ties VPC endpoints to route tables for lower cross-AZ cost and improved resiliency, and (4) provides hooks and probes to run safe upgrades with minimal blast radius.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Provide one reusable Terraform module (and minimal wrapper examples) that can be consumed by customer infra or Redwood on-prem templates.
- Module supports: subnet tiers (control, services, workloads), explicit AZ mapping, per-subnet route table attachment, and tag-based role assignment.
- Egress abstraction: configurable to use NAT Gateways (managed or shared), IGW, or an egress appliance; automatically creates HA egress across AZs and exposes a failover policy.
- VPC Endpoints: Create interface/gateway endpoints with endpoint affinity rules (prefer local-AZ endpoints), health-checked route selection, and endpoint policy attachments.
- Upgrade hooks: allow pre/post hooks (null_resource triggers) and safe rollout patterns (canary AZ, synthetic probes that validate cross-AZ connectivity, and automatic route rollback on probe failures).
- Built-in synthetic health checks published to the Console metrics pipeline for visibility.
- Comprehensive terraform plan/apply unit tests and an integration test in a sandbox account.

Proposed design and components:
1) Module layout
   - modules/subnet-tier: creates subnet groups with configurable prefix sizing, AZ mapping, and role tags.
   - modules/egress-abstraction: creates NATs/IGWs/egress appliance resources and a canonical egress route table per AZ, with cross-AZ failover policy and optional central egress configuration.
   - modules/endpoint-manager: creates VPC endpoints, attaches endpoint policies, and populates route tables with endpoint affinity rules.
   - modules/upgrade-hooks: exposes null_resource hooks and a small Lambda (optional) that runs synthetic checks and reports status to CloudWatch/Console.

2) Route orchestration and tagging
   - Each subnet receives a role tag (rw:subnet-role=control|service|workload) and an az tag. Route tables are generated per role+AZ and attached to subnets accordingly.
   - Endpoint affinity implemented by preferring endpoint IPs that are in the same AZ (via route table entries and health probe weights).

3) Health checks & probes
   - Lightweight synthetic probe that validates: endpoint DNS resolution, TCP handshake to endpoint ENI, and sample egress path via NAT/IGW.
   - Probe frequency and alerting configurable; failures trigger a rollback plan (terraform apply with previous route table config) or a toggle to mark an AZ as degraded.

4) Upgrade strategy
   - Canary AZ: upgrade or reapply changes one AZ at a time. After each AZ apply, run synthetic probes; if failures > threshold, automatically pause and emit rollback playbook.
   - Drift detection: run pre-apply plan which runs a module-level linter to catch risky changes (e.g., CIDR shrink, route purges).

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Complexity vs. flexibility: Introduces opinionated defaults (per-AZ route tables, default endpoint affinity) to reduce customer footguns, but provides knobs to opt out.
- Central NAT vs distributed NAT: default to distributed per-AZ NAT for resilience and bandwidth scaling; provide option for central NAT to reduce IP costs for small installs.
- Use of Lambda for probes vs pure Terraform null_resource: Lambda preferred for continuous probes and minimal state in terraform. null_resource used only for upgrade hook triggers.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests with Terratest: subnet sizing, tag propagation, route table attach/detach semantics.
- Integration sandbox: automated end-to-end deploy into a test AWS account using the sample overlay; run synthetic probes and failover exercises (simulate AZ fail by deregistering endpoint ENIs).
- Canary rollout verification checklist documented in Confluence and linked in PR.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge module into infra/modules with feature flag support.
2) Deploy to internal sandbox and run integration suite.
3) Run private customer pilot with 1-2 internal customers (Platform team and Solutions Eng).
4) Publish module registry entry and update private-deploy templates.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- Terraform module has complete README, examples, and CHANGELOG.
- Integration tests pass in sandbox account and synthetic probe metrics are visible in Console.
- Upgrade hooks exercised during canary deploys with documented rollbacks.
- Security review completed and KMS/HSM usage for any probe secrets verified.

Open questions / next decisions:
- Cross-account VPC endpoint patterns for enterprise customers with centralized endpoints: integrate now or follow-up?
- Standard naming/tagging convention alignment with infra registry (need to confirm with Infra Org).
- Should we include an optional centralized egress router appliance blueprint (NGFW)? This may increase scope and is likely a follow-up.

Links / artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/VPC+Networking+Module+PRD
- Design notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vpc-networking-design
- Example overlay repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/tree/main/examples/vpc-overlay
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234

Security & compliance notes:
- Ensure endpoint policies and S3 access through gateway endpoints follow least privilege.
- KMS keys for probes and any Lambda secrets must be customer-managed where required by Private deployments.
